Author: Lalitha Kanneganti
Bench: Lalitha Kanneganti
 The Honourable Smt. Justice Lalitha Kanneganti
 M.A.C.M.A.Nos.325 of 2009 and 1024 of 2008
Common Judgment

:
Aggrieved by the award dated 31.03.2007 in O.P.No.1383 of 2003 passed by the Chairman, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Dist.Judge), Nizamabad, the A.P.S.R.T.C. has filed M.A.C.M.A No.325 of 2009, questioning the compensation and the claimants have filed MACMA No.1024 of 2008 seeking enhancement of the compensation.
2. Having heard both sides, perused the entire material on record.
3. The claim petition was filed seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- on account the death of the deceased in motor vehicle accident.
4.

The case of the claimants is that on 01.12.2001, while the deceased, who was working as conductor in A.P.S.R.T.C., was standing by the side of the bus stop and giving return change to the passengers, at about 11.20 a.m., a bus belonging to the respondent corporation being driven by its driver in high speed in rash and negligent manner has dashed the deceased, due to which, the deceased sustained multiple grievous injuries and he was shifted to Government Hospital, where he was died at 11.45 a.m. 2

5. Learned counsel appearing for A.P.S.R.T.C submits that the claimants by way of Ex.P13 i.e., a letter dated 10.12.2021 filed a petition before the Depot Manager, A.P.S.R.T.C, to arrange to pay workmen's compensation as per the Rules.
It is the further stated that they have not filed any petition before any Court as they have approached under Workmen's Compensation Act.
6. According to the A.P.S.R.T.C, they are not entitled for any compensation under the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988.

The Tribunal having discussed various Judgments of the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that the claimants though filed an application, the Corporation has assessed compensation of Rs.1,46,200/- under the Workmen's Compensation Act and submitted same to the Commissioner.
Accordingly, the Court below has deducted an amount of Rs.1,46,200/- from Rs.8,09,204/- and granted compensation of Rs.6,63,004/-.

7. Learned counsel for A.P.S.R.T.C. submitted that in the light of the bar under Section 167 of the Motor Vehicle Act, the claimants cannot simultaneously approach the Tribunal under the Motor Aziza Begum And 5 Others vs Andhra Pradesh State Road Transport ... on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149888840/
1 Vehicle Act as well as under the Workmen's Compensation Act.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal deducting the amount that is assessed under the Workmen's Compensation Act and granting compensation of Rs.6,63,004/- was wrong.

Learned counsel for the claimants submitted that this Act being a beneficial legislation and due to wrong advise they have addressed a letter to the Depot Manager as there is nothing forth coming to show that they have claimed compensation.
As the claimants have lost the deceased they are entitled for compensation under the Motor Vehicle Act and compensation granted by the Tribunal is not a reasonable compensation.
9. The deceased was working as a conductor in A.P.S.R.T.C.

The wife of the deceased has addressed a letter to the Depot manager seeking compensation under the Workmen's Compensation Act and they have also filed assessed compensation at Rs.1,46,200/- and simultaneously, an application was filed under the Motor Vehicle Act.

The Tribunal considering these facts has deducted Rs.1,46,200/-
and granted remaining amount of Rs.6,63,004/- from the arrived compensation of Rs.8,09,204/-.
On the face of it, the said award passed by the Tribunal was wrong.

10. When the Tribunal has appreciated the fact that there is an application before the Workmen's Compensation Act, the Court below ought not to have entertained that application under Motor Vehicle Act and further ought not to have apportioned the amount.
In the light of the same, the award passed by the Tribunal is set aside.
The claimants cannot maintain an application both under the Motor Vehicle Act and under the Workmen's Compensation Act.

12. In view of the same, the claimants are only entitled for the compensation under the Workmen's Compensation Act and accordingly the appeal of the claimants i.e., M.A.C.M.A.No.1024 of 2008 is dismissed and the appeal of the A.P.S.R.T.C. i.e., M.A.C.M.A.No.325 of 2009 is allowed.

Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
___________________________ LALITHA KANNEGANTI, J Date: 19.06.2023 sa/vsl 5 LK,J MACMA_325_2009 & MACMA_1024_2008 THE HONOURABLE SMT. JUSTICE
